lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Raise a concern about the anchor or lifeline
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Stop work and ask the competent person to confirm the site-specific setup.

words.en: Use the roof anchor — don't freelance.
Stop work. The anchor is not safe.
Confirm the anchor setup before we continue.

readingEnglish: While they work on the roof, a worker sees something wrong with the lifeline.
He stops and tells the foreman.
The foreman says: Stop work. The anchor is not safe.
The foreman asks: Where is the competent person?
Check whether the lifeline has any damage.
The competent person does the inspection and confirms the fall distance of the system.
Confirm the anchor setup before we continue.
A harness is no use if the anchor or the lanyard fails.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Stop work. The anchor is not safe.
Check whether the lifeline has any damage.
The competent person confirms the fall distance of the system.
The worker stops and tells the foreman.
A harness is no use if the anchor or the lanyard fails.

lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Warn about slippery conditions and changing weather
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Warn the crew about slick footing and bring them down when lightning approaches.

words.en: Watch your footing — the dew is slick.
Don't work the roof in lightning.
Stop work and come down if the weather changes.
The roof is wet. Be careful.
A storm is coming. Come down now.

readingEnglish: It is 6:30 in the morning and there is still dew on the roof.
The foreman warns: The roof is wet. Be careful.
Look for solid footing, because the dew makes the roof slippery.
Wear boots with good grip.
Later, the wind picks up and dark clouds appear in the sky.
Do not work the roof in lightning.
The foreman shouts: A storm is coming. Come down now.
Stop work and come down if the weather changes.

verbs.exampleEnglish: A storm is coming. Come down now.
Stop work and come down if the weather changes.
We look for solid footing because the dew is slick.
Come down if the weather changes.

lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Check on crew hydration and heat symptoms
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: Ask a worker how they feel and direct a water break under the site heat plan.

words.en: Take a water break every hour.
Go to the shade and rest.
Tell me if you feel sick.

readingEnglish: It is very hot and the sun beats down on the roof.
The foreman says: Take a water break every hour.
But Raúl does not look well, and the foreman walks over.
The foreman asks him: How do you feel?
Are you dizzy?
Raúl answers yes, a little.
The foreman tells him: Go to the shade and rest. Drink water now.
Tell me if you feel sick, and we will follow the site heat plan.
Hydration and rest in the shade help prevent heat exhaustion.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Raúl rests in the shade because he feels dizzy.

verbs.meaningEnglish: to let know, to tell, to notify
verbs.exampleEnglish: Raúl tells the foreman if he feels sick.
Raúl goes to the shade to rest.
